title: “ENOUGH!” anti-corruption and COVID-management protest in Nicosia
location: Kolokasis Park and central Nicosia; report also describes police action along Makarios Avenue.
scope: Local gathering; the article directs demands at the government managing the pandemic and refers to the Greek Cypriot political system. Exact administrative boundary coding and the broader island coverage scope remain for coordinator review.
organizer: The article calls it an “ENOUGH!” protest organized by many groups and organizations; it does not enumerate their names.
threshold_50_evidence: Cyprus Mail reports an event-specific estimate of around 300–400 participants. It separately says large groups were prevented from reaching the main protest; those groups are not added to the reported count.

occurrence.summary: Cyprus Mail’s same-day report describes the Nicosia “ENOUGH!” protest.

start_date.summary: The article dates the march to Saturday 13 February 2021.

end_date.summary: It says the gathering ended around 90 minutes after its start; both reported times fall on 13 February. Exact end time is not given.

location.summary: The report places the start at Kolokasis Park in old Nicosia and describes the later dispersal along Makarios Avenue.

organizer.summary: The article labels it the “ENOUGH!” protest and says many groups and organizations organized it; it names no individual organizer in the read text.

demands.summary: The article describes demands against corruption, state authoritarianism/censorship, and government management of the pandemic.

participants_original.summary: The article reports around 300–400 participants at the main protest; it separately notes other groups were prevented from reaching it.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported estimate of around 300–400 at this specific event exceeds 50.

protester_violence.summary: The report mentions altercations with police but does not identify violence by protesters; retain unknown.

state_response.summary: The report says at least eight people were arrested; a protester alleges pepper-spraying and beatings against some marchers; police used water cannon and tear gas to disperse the crowd. No evidence in this report establishes accommodation, official ignoring, killings, or shootings.

notes: One body-read source supports an event-specific turnout above 50 and demands directed at Cyprus government policy. Alleged police beatings are participant-attributed in this source, not independently verified. Keep this physical gathering distinct from the 20 February Nicosia action; its relationship to that later “Os Dame” event/campaign is unresolved because no February 20 article body has been read. Other Cyprus jurisdictional coverage is not inferred.
